title: WP-VER close-out: the G08 ladder's institutional learning, and the five demands it discharges
objective: Close out the badf-engineering-verification program (VER-A..E, e1423ad -> d292801, now ACTIVE) by recording its one substantive institutional learning and discharging its five demands against it. The learning -- docs/learnings/a-guard-that-cannot-fail-is-not-a-guard.md -- names the defect class behind every defect the program shipped or nearly shipped: a check pointed at a PROXY for its property (a comment character, a seat name in any body, a dict key, a line, a status field, a pipeline's last exit code) rather than at the property itself, so the proxy can occur without the property holding and vice versa. Instances are recorded across ALL FOUR seats unqualified, because the class is a property of the work and not of one agent's care. BADF-REV's generalization and its two mitigations (assert the property directly; give every guard a positive control that has been seen to fail -- a guard never observed red is not evidence) are credited to them. BADF-DEM-0087/0090/0092/0093/0095 flip AUTHORIZED -> RESOLVED referencing that file. The VER-E doctrine section gains the #217 link, discharging the carried intent recorded in #217's body.
business_value: A ladder that produced five landed rungs and six distinct near-misses teaches one thing worth keeping, and BADF's own doctrine says a concluded demand must state it or explicitly state that there is none. Discharging five demands with a real learning -- rather than the bulk NONE_DECLARED refused on #220 -- is the template for how the other 81 should eventually be discharged: at each demand's natural moment, with something actually learned.
